{{Short description|Proposed restrictions on developing artificial superintelligence}}

A '''superintelligence ban''' refers to proposed legal, ethical, or policy measures intended to restrict or prohibit the development of [[artificial superintelligence]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Scammell |first=Robert |date=October 22, 2025 |title=Prince Harry, Steve Bannon, and will.i.am join tech pioneers calling for an AI superintelligence ban |url=https://www.businessinsider.com/ai-superintelligence-ban-tech-business-leaders-steve-bannon-richard-branson-2025-10 |access-date=2025-10-23 |website=[[Business Insider]] |language=en-US}}</ref> AI systems that would surpass human cognitive abilities in nearly all domains.<ref name="Butts-2025">{{Cite web |last=Butts |first=Dylan |date=October 22, 2025 |title=Hundreds of public figures, including Apple co-founder Steve Wozniak and Virgin's Richard Branson urge AI ‘superintelligence’ ban |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2025/10/22/800-petition-signatures-apple-steve-wozniak-and-virgin-richard-branson-superintelligence-race.html |access-date=2025-10-23 |website=[[CNBC]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Ray |first=Siladitya |title=Harry And Meghan, Steve Bannon And More Sign Petition Urging AI ‘Superintelligence’ Ban |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/siladityaray/2025/10/22/public-figures-sign-petition-urging-ban-on-ai-superintelligence-including-harry-meghan-steve-bannon-and-richard-branson/ |access-date=2025-10-23 |website=[[Forbes]] |language=en}}</ref> The idea arises from concerns that such systems could become uncontrollable, potentially posing [[existential risk from artificial general intelligence|existential threats]] to humanity or causing severe social and economic disruption.<ref name="Butts-2025" /><ref name="The Economic Times-2025">{{Cite web |date=September 10, 2025 |title=Are we living in a computer simulation? Philosopher behind the theory issues an eerie new warning on AI: ‘We would find different bases for our self-worth’ - The Economic Times |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/magazines/panache/simulation-theory-prediction-nick-bostrom-new-ai-superintelligence-warning-complete-unemployment-different-self-worth-and-dignity/articleshow/123808369.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2025-10-23 |website=[[The Economic Times]]}}</ref>

== Background ==
The concept of limiting or banning superintelligence research has roots in early 21st-century debates on [[artificial general intelligence]] (AGI) safety. Thinkers such as [[Nick Bostrom]] and [[Eliezer Yudkowsky]] warned that self-improving AI could rapidly exceed human oversight.<ref name="The Economic Times-2025" /><ref>{{Cite news |last=Adams |first=Tim |date=June 12, 2016 |title=Artificial intelligence: ‘We’re like children playing with a bomb’ |url=https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2016/jun/12/nick-bostrom-artificial-intelligence-machine |access-date=2025-10-23 |work=[[The Guardian]] |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> As advanced models like large-scale [[language model|language models]] and [[autonomous agent|autonomous agents]] began demonstrating complex reasoning abilities, policymakers and ethicists increasingly discussed the need for legal constraints on the creation of systems capable of [[recursive self-improvement]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-10-22 |title=Many big names in group of unlikely allies seeking ban, for now, on AI "superintelligence" |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/prince-harry-steve-bannon-unlikely-allies-ai-superintelligence-ban/ |access-date=2025-10-23 |website=[[CBS News]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

In October 2025, the [[Future of Life Institute]] published a statement<ref>{{Cite web |title=Statement on Superintelligence |url=https://superintelligence-statement.org/ |access-date=2026-01-25 |website=superintelligence-statement.org |language=en}}</ref> calling for "a prohibition on the development of superintelligence, not lifted before there is broad scientific consensus that it will be done safely and controllably, and strong public buy-in." This statement was signed by various public personalities, such as [[Richard Branson]] and [[Steve Wozniak]], and AI experts, such as [[Yoshua Bengio]] and [[Geoffrey Hinton]].<ref name="Butts-2025" />

== Rationale ==
Supporters of a superintelligence ban argue that once AI systems surpass human intelligence, traditional containment, alignment, and control methods may fail. They contend that even limited experimentation with such systems could lead to irreversible outcomes, including loss of human decision-making power or unintended global harm. Some propose international treaties modeled after the [[Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons|nuclear non-proliferation framework]] to prevent a competitive [[AI arms race]].<ref name="Butts-2025" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Perrigo |first=Billy |last2=Pillay |first2=Tharin |date=October 22, 2025 |title=Open Letter Calls for Ban on Superintelligent AI Development |url=https://time.com/7327409/ai-agi-superintelligent-open-letter/ |access-date=2025-10-23 |website=[[Time (magazine)|Time]] |language=en}}</ref>

Opponents argue that a ban would be difficult to define and enforce, given the lack of a precise threshold distinguishing advanced AGI from superintelligence. They also warn that excessive restriction could slow scientific progress, hinder beneficial automation, and encourage unregulated underground research.<ref name="Butts-2025" /><ref>{{Cite news |title=Google's ex-CEO Eric Schmidt says America is ill-equipped to address AI's 'biggest challenge' |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/technology/tech-news/googles-ex-ceo-eric-schmidt-says-america-is-ill-equipped-to-address-ais-biggest-challenge/articleshow/122782157.cms |access-date=2025-10-23 |work=[[The Times of India]] |issn=0971-8257}}</ref>

== Global discussion ==
Although no government has enacted an explicit superintelligence ban, the idea has been debated within the [[European Union]], [[United Nations]], and several independent [[AI safety]] organizations. The [[Future of Life Institute]], [[Center for AI Safety]], and other organizations have called for international cooperation to manage risks associated with the pursuit of superintelligent systems.{{Citation needed|date=January 2026}} In 2024 and 2025, proposals for a temporary moratorium on frontier AI research were circulated among major technology firms and research institutes, reflecting growing public concern over the trajectory of AI capabilities.<ref name="Butts-2025" />
